Why doesn't the following command actually end xorg while in terminal in GUI? With the latest release of ubuntu mate:

sudo pkill -15 xorg

If I do it from any other line xorg will stop, but not when I am in the GUI. I don't proclaim to be an expert, but want to be. Care to share?
Several upvoats with no replies...Does no one use pkill, or is it that not enough people have the ability to downvoat yet?

Does "pgrep xorg" return a number for you? And if what process does that number refer to in "ps ax"?

Sorry, I am a bit guessing here...but the process of the xserver is not called "xorg" usually and rather just "X". Of course that could be different on your distro. Interesting is though that you say it works outside of Xorg. Does that mean if you are not logged in and only the display manager is running or does it also work if you are logged in a graphical environment and switch to a TTY and use it from there?

I think the actual X server process is just called x - capital x.

Open an terminal window and try: sudo killall -9 X

If that doesn't work, try holding the ctrl and alt keys down and pressing aone of F2 through F6 to open a "virtual terminal." You'll have to login at the prompt, then try the 'sudo killall -9 X' command again.

Good luck!
Yes, i am able to use it with any of the other Virtual lines. I'm just wondering why it is that it would work within the GUI. I didn't realize I might be able to just kill X. So many thinkings.

No no no no no.

Please, please, please, do NOT use -9/SIGKILL unless absolutely necessary. It doesn't allow to the program to exit cleanly which can be a very bad thing.

Use SIGTERM/-15. If that doesn't work use SIGINT/-1. If that doesn't work, then and only then, use SIGKILL
I always use 15 before 9, but wasn't aware of 1. Thanks.
IIRC, 15 is Ctrl-C, 1 is closing your terminal and 9 is murdering the process with a chainsaw.

If I need to kill xorg I go to another TTY and run 'killall xinit'. Probably totally wrong way to do it, and I should educate myself on levels and whatnot, but it does the job. One punch and X is down.

btw. I don't run a display manager and starts my gui worlds from .xinitrc.
If you want to kill xorg, why not just Ctrl-Alt-Backspace? That will shut it down and drop you back to your original terminal or display manager (kdm, gdm, etc).
